_doc: Which supplier parts each head-carrier screw post is made of (Idle T-5bqc3m). Post positions are never typed: robot/body/neck-head/head_holes.py measures the bore of the named spacer / shim / terminal nut on its mesh in the shell-pass manifest (defined_holes.SHELL_PASS), where the supplier parts sit as supplied. group: screw family of the post; spacers / terminals / screws: manifest part names in post order (screw names get the chosen length, M2_ -> M2x<L>_); washers (camera): the supplier washers whose board-side face is the board's front face (the head seat); legacy_screws: manifest parts the generated screws replace; drop: supplier parts the printed features replace; head: standard and thread of the screw (dk / k / lengths from robot/body/checks/data/hardware.json screw_standards; a standard that table does not carry gives dk / k / lengths here, with its source). Only catalogue hardware in standard sizes (owner 2026-11-22): ISO screws, ISO washers, ISO 4032 nuts, catalogue heat-set inserts; no steel rings. compute (T-5bqc3m K2): ISO 4762 M2.5 hex socket head on an ISO 7092 small washer (washer) on the carrier front, through a plain hole_dia clearance hole (ISO 273 medium), the spacer / ROCK4D / fan bridge into the supplier nut (terminal); the length is the smallest ISO 4762 length whose thread ends at least engagement_margin_mm past the nut's far face. Where no standard length reaches with the washer on the plate front (the fan-bridge posts: 25.5 mm from the front face to the nut's far face, ISO 4762 M2.5 stops at 25), the supplier spacer is replaced by a printed column (column: its radius, gap_mm short of the board, a base of base_ro round the counterbore) and the washer sits in a counterbore (washer d2 + 2 x counterbore_clear_mm) whose floor puts the longest standard length engagement_margin_mm past the far face. neck_root (K2): the 2 M3 screws joining the carrier to the neck pitch-to-head cradle tongue: ISO 7380-1 M3 button head on the carrier's rear face (6.0 mm pitch: an ISO 10642 M3 countersink (dk 6.72) or an ISO 7089 / 7092 washer (OD 7.0 / 6.0) does not fit between the two), plain hole_dia hole (ISO 273 medium), through the cradle's steel sleeve into an ISO 4032 M3 nut on the cradle's front face (flats facing each other along z, 0.5 mm apart); head_clear_mm: radial clearance of the head; the dorsal rib it sits in is cut in a square window of half-width rib_window_half_mm round the axis (across the rib's whole width, x -3.5..2.1: a round cut left a 0.35 mm strip of rib beside the head). camera (owner 2026-11-22: only catalogue hardware, printable and hand-assemblable): the 8 supplier F-F standoffs are replaced by a printed column (column.ro 3.0 at the plate: 1.4 mm rim round the 3.2 mm insert hole; column.height 4.97 = the standoff's 5 mm less 0.03 mm so the board face never overlaps the column in the fit check; the screw clamp closes it) on the carrier plate with a clearance bore (column.bore_dia). Where components on the board's back stand next to the post the column is narrower (T-5bqc3m K1): head_holes.column_profile measures the board's mesh round each post and gives each height band the radius that keeps column.component_clear_mm to the nearest component, never less than column.rim_mm round the bore (column.insert_rim_mm round the insert), widening toward the plate in 45 deg steps (printable with the plate on the bed), steps under column.min_step_mm merged into the wider band. A catalogue M2 x 3 brass heat-set insert is pushed from the plate's rear face (before ROCK4D goes on) up to the bore's ledge; the insert's rear end is flush with the plate's rear face (the heated tip ends on that face), its front end on the column bore's ledge; the ISO 4762 M2 screw is driven from the camera front through board and column into it, the smallest standard length that reaches the 1 d reference with its point inside the insert. The ribs behind the plate keep a square window of half-width press_clear_mm round each insert axis free for the heated tip (rib ends cut square, no slivers; 4.8 = the 8 mm tip's 4.0 + the 0.6 mm root fillet of the cut rib end + 0.2: at 4.4 the fillet stood 0.04 mm3 in the tip's way at insert 7). mic (owner 2026-11-22: one screw, a printed retention instead of the upper screw; T-5bqc3m review: every step by hand on the bench): the board sits on a printed wing of the carrier (wing.face_gap_mm behind its back face, wing.t_mm thick, top wing.top_z_mm, thinned to wing.taper_t_mm above wing.taper_z_mm where the head skin closes in); one catalogue M2 x 3 brass heat-set insert in a boss on the wing's skin side (boss.ro; its underside and the insert hole's top are 45 deg teardrops along boss.teardrop_down, the print direction's down, so the horizontal boss prints without support), pushed from the boss's free end (+x, carrier alone on the bench) up to a printed floor; the floor is as thick as the screw needs: the insert's front end goes where the standard screw length reaches engagement_target_mm (the smallest length that leaves a floor of at least floor_min_mm), the insert's rear end is the boss end. The ISO 14580 M2 hexalobular cheese head (T6, k 1.3: clear of ROCK4D; ISO 7380-1 starts at M3, an ISO 7045 pan head k 1.6 would leave 0.1 mm) is driven from the board side through the PCB and the floor's clearance bore (bore_dia) before ROCK4D goes on, so mic and cable are fitted before the skin. A printed locating pin (pin.dia, pin.length into the PCB) on the wing face goes into the board's second mounting hole (the bore of drop[1], 2.43 mm measured) and keeps it from turning about the screw; port: the acoustic port relief through the wing (robot/model/build/contracts.py microphone_port). Insert: catalogue-class brass knurled heat-set insert M2 x 3.0 mm, knurl OD 3.6 mm, recommended hole 3.2 mm (CNC Kitchen / Ruthex M2 x 3 class; ASSUMPTION: no supplier data in the repo, hole size from the manufacturers' published tables, not checked against a data sheet here); modelled as a tube of the hole diameter (sleeve.ro) with the thread's minor diameter as bore (no overlap check against the melted-in plastic). threads: ISO 724 M2 major / minor diameter (same values as torso_screws.THREADS). ASSUMPTIONS: thread modelled at the minor diameter; 1 d engagement for a steel screw in a brass thread (robot/actuators/interfaces/standard-parts.json lists 1.5 d for brass: 3.0 mm, the insert's length).

washer.source: ISO 7092 (small series, 200 HV) M2.5: d1 2.7, d2 5.0, h 0.5 (transcribed from the standard's table, not re-checked against the text; robot/body/checks/data/hardware.json carries no washer standard)

head.source: ISO 14580:2011 hexalobular socket cheese head M2 (T6): dk max 3.8, k max 1.3, lengths 3-20 (transcribed from the standard's table, not re-checked against the text); not in robot/body/checks/data/hardware.json

boss.teardrop_note: down in the carrier's print direction (process up -y in build_neck_head_connectors.bom.yaml, seeded)

threads._doc: ISO 724 M2: major 2.0, minor 1.567 (the heat-set insert's modelled bore); same as torso_screws.THREADS (T-bv7bwe).
